alerts.title: Carbamazepine–DTG interaction causing viral breakthrough
alerts.message: Guidelines list carbamazepine as a contraindication for DTG because carbamazepine decreases DTG levels by 30–70%. The patient started carbamazepine 2 weeks ago, and viral load rose from <50 to 1,240 copies/mL despite reported good adherence. The clinician's plan does not address this interaction. Reduced DTG exposure is the most likely cause of the new viremia. The plan to reduce carbamazepine dose will not resolve the interaction.

evidence.recommended_action: Switch carbamazepine to valproic acid or another non-enzyme-inducing antiepileptic, or switch DTG to an unaffected ARV. Repeat viral load after adjusting therapy.

alerts.title: Detectable viral load requires adherence support and repeat testing
alerts.message: Viral load of 1,240 copies/mL exceeds the >200 copies/mL threshold associated with risk of treatment failure. Guidelines recommend enhanced adherence support and repeat viral load testing after addressing the drug interaction. The current plan only addresses carbamazepine toxicity and does not include adherence counselling or a follow-up viral load strategy.

evidence.recommended_action: Provide enhanced adherence support, resolve the carbamazepine–DTG interaction, and repeat viral load in 3 months per guideline algorithm.

alerts.title: Mild ALT elevation with TDF and hepatotoxic co-medications
alerts.message: ALT is 68 U/L with mild elevation. TDF can cause hepatotoxicity; guidelines recommend LFTs when liver-related symptoms arise. However, the elevation is modest and carbamazepine and valproate are both known hepatotoxins, making either anticonvulsant a more likely cause. The patient has no reported hepatitis symptoms. Ongoing LFT monitoring is warranted.

evidence.recommended_action: Repeat LFTs with next blood draw. If ALT rises further, evaluate valproate and carbamazepine as primary hepatotoxic suspects before attributing to TDF.
